world.title: Israel warns of preemptive strike over alleged Iranian chemical weapons effort
world.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz accused Iran of developing chemical weapons on Tuesday and said Israel would prevent Tehran from acquiring the capability to use them. Katz said Iran could not yet attack Israel with such weapons but raised the possibility of a preemptive strike if Israeli intelligence indicated Ira
world.content: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz accused Iran of developing chemical weapons on Tuesday and said Israel would prevent Tehran from acquiring the capability to use them. Katz said Iran could not yet attack Israel with such weapons but raised the possibility of a preemptive strike if Israeli intelligence indicated Iran was planning an attack. Katz said Israel and the United States had intelligence about the alleged effort; Israeli reports also said information had been shared with Gulf countries. He did not specify where the program was operating or how far it had advanced, according to one report. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi rejected a separate report about an alleged Iranian dirty-bomb plot against U.S. officials as “Iraq War-style propaganda”; Iran has also denied developing chemical weapons. Israel’s opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who has been asked to form a government after an inconclusive election, said he saw no immediate reason for an attack before a new government was formed. Katz said Israeli and U.S. forces were preparing for a possible strike, while President Donald Trump would decide on any U.S. military action.

world.title: Trump prepares new tariffs on 16 economies after subsidies probe
world.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration is preparing new tariffs on 16 economies, including China, India, the European Union, Japan and South Korea, after a months-long U.S. investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity and subsidies. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office was expected to release its findings a
world.content: President Donald Trump’s administration is preparing new tariffs on 16 economies, including China, India, the European Union, Japan and South Korea, after a months-long U.S. investigation into alleged excess industrial capacity and subsidies. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office was expected to release its findings as soon as Wednesday, Nov. 25, though people familiar with the plans said the timing could change. The administration would impose the proposed duties under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, partly replacing broad tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. The new duties would be added to separate tariffs of 10% to 12.5% imposed in July over alleged failures to prevent imports made with forced labor; those tariffs also face a court challenge. Final rates have not been announced. The administration is expected to observe tariff caps in existing trade agreements. After releasing its proposed findings, it will hold hearings and decide on final duties; Indian officials expect that process to take about 45 days.
world.image_alt: Trump prepares new tariffs on 16 economies after subsidies probe

world.title: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot wins first coalition pact, majority remains elusive
world.summary: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief who leads the centre-right Yashar party, agreed to sign the first coalition pact since Israel’s Oct. 27 election with Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Israel Our Home party. The deal gives Eisenkot a partner but not a majority: his bloc holds 48 seats in the 120-member Kness
world.content: Gadi Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief who leads the centre-right Yashar party, agreed to sign the first coalition pact since Israel’s Oct. 27 election with Avigdor Lieberman’s right-wing Israel Our Home party. The deal gives Eisenkot a partner but not a majority: his bloc holds 48 seats in the 120-member Knesset, Israel’s parliament, while the alliance backing caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has 53. Parties representing Israel’s Arab minority hold 19 seats and could support Eisenkot, but Lieberman has opposed relying on them. The parties remain divided over the makeup of a government. The left-wing Democrats party, led by Yair Golan, suspended talks with Yashar, citing progress in unity-government discussions between Eisenkot and Netanyahu’s Likud party and deadlock over forming a government without Netanyahu. Eisenkot could also seek support from ultra-Orthodox parties; negotiations with United Torah Judaism have focused on arrests for draft evasion and the enlistment of ultra-Orthodox men. President Isaac Herzog gave Eisenkot a 28-day mandate to form a government, running through Dec. 6, with the possibility of a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu can try to form a government; if neither succeeds, Israel is expected to hold another election next year.
world.image_alt: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot wins first coalition pact, majority remains elusive

world.title: Ukraine
world.summary: Two Libyan naval personnel died of wounds sustained in Ukraine’s acknowledged naval-drone operation against two Russian vessels at and near Benghazi on Nov. 22, eastern Libyan authorities said. Kyiv said it struck the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi’s naval base and the cargo ship MV Angara offshore; President Vol
world.content: Two Libyan naval personnel died of wounds sustained in Ukraine’s acknowledged naval-drone operation against two Russian vessels at and near Benghazi on Nov. 22, eastern Libyan authorities said. Kyiv said it struck the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi’s naval base and the cargo ship MV Angara offshore; President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said seven Ukrainian-made sea drones took part. Ukraine said the corvette sank, while reports said the cargo vessel was hit. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attacks self-defense against Russian aggression and said vessels carrying military supplies were legitimate targets. Libya’s internationally recognized government in Tripoli condemned the operation, denied any agreement with Kyiv and said Libya would not accept being drawn into the war. The eastern Libyan administration also condemned the strike; its Libyan National Army (LNA) said a response would come “at the appropriate time and place”. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Sybiha that Rome had not been informed and urged efforts to prevent the conflict from spreading into the Mediterranean. The UN mission in Libya called for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation.

world.title: US grand jury adds second child sexual abuse material charge against Meghan Markle
world.summary: A federal grand jury in Los Angeles indicted Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, on Nov. 24 on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material, up from a single federal charge filed earlier this month. Prosecutors allege he knowingly possessed 35mm negatives containing ille
world.content: A federal grand jury in Los Angeles indicted Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Meghan Markle, the Duchess of Sussex, on Nov. 24 on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material, up from a single federal charge filed earlier this month. Prosecutors allege he knowingly possessed 35mm negatives containing illegal images; the indictment says at least one image involved a prepubescent child and a child under 12. The investigation followed reports of suspected child sexual abuse material in the Philippines, where Markle previously lived. Authorities say they found suspected images in two Los Angeles storage units. Philippine police have filed separate complaints alleging possession and distribution offences. Markle denies possessing the material. Markle, 82, remains in federal custody in Florida after authorities say he removed an electronic monitoring device. A judge has ruled him competent to stand trial, and prosecutors expect him to be transferred to California for arraignment in Los Angeles in the coming weeks. Each federal count carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison if he is convicted.
world.image_alt: US grand jury adds second child sexual abuse material charge against Meghan Markle

world.title: Salvadoran migrant leaves U.S. for Spain after deportation fight
world.summary: Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadoran migrant whose mistaken deportation became a test of President Donald Trump’s immigration policy, left the United States for Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday, Nov. 24, after a judge set a deadline for him to depart. The Department of Homeland Security called it a self-deportation u
world.content: Kilmar Ábrego García, a Salvadoran migrant whose mistaken deportation became a test of President Donald Trump’s immigration policy, left the United States for Spain on a commercial flight Tuesday, Nov. 24, after a judge set a deadline for him to depart. The Department of Homeland Security called it a self-deportation under a removal order; his lawyers described it as a negotiated, temporary departure and said he may be able to return. The government has not publicly detailed the agreement’s terms. The case began after U.S. officials sent Ábrego García to El Salvador in March 2025 despite a 2019 court order barring his return because of gang threats. The administration later called the deportation an administrative error and brought him back in June 2025 after the Supreme Court ordered it to facilitate his return. A federal judge dismissed human-smuggling charges in May 2026, finding the prosecution vindictive; the Justice Department appealed. After his return, officials pursued deportation to several African countries, most recently Liberia, while Ábrego García sought to go to Costa Rica. The appeal of the dismissal of his criminal case remains pending, with arguments scheduled in February.
world.image_alt: Salvadoran migrant leaves U.S. for Spain after deportation fight

world.title: Colombian forces rescue all hostages after Cartagena supermarket siege
world.summary: Colombian security forces rescued all hostages from an Éxito supermarket in Cartagena early Wednesday, ending a nearly 17-hour standoff that began when armed men fled into the store after a failed armored-car robbery. President Abelardo de la Espriella said one hostage-taker was killed in the raid; officials had not re
world.content: Colombian security forces rescued all hostages from an Éxito supermarket in Cartagena early Wednesday, ending a nearly 17-hour standoff that began when armed men fled into the store after a failed armored-car robbery. President Abelardo de la Espriella said one hostage-taker was killed in the raid; officials had not released details about the rescued hostages’ condition. The gunmen initially seized about 30 people on Tuesday morning. Police said 10 were freed during negotiations before troops and police stormed the building. Explosions were heard shortly before security forces entered. The hostage crisis followed a car bombing late Monday in Villavicencio that injured more than 20 people and damaged homes and businesses. The government blamed dissidents of the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) for the bombing; the supermarket hostage-taking was not attributed to an armed group. The rescue came on the 10th anniversary of the 2016 peace accord with the FARC.
world.image_alt: Colombian forces rescue all hostages after Cartagena supermarket siege

world.title: Two men arrested after suspected break-in at Prince William’s Norfolk home
world.summary: Police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after responding to a report of suspicious activity at the Sandringham estate in Norfolk on Monday evening, Nov. 23. Norfolk Police said officers searched the area with police dogs, drones and a helicopter. The men remained in custody on Tuesday and had not
world.content: Police arrested two men on suspicion of burglary and trespass after responding to a report of suspicious activity at the Sandringham estate in Norfolk on Monday evening, Nov. 23. Norfolk Police said officers searched the area with police dogs, drones and a helicopter. The men remained in custody on Tuesday and had not been charged. British media identified the property as Anmer Hall, Prince William and Princess Catherine’s 10-bedroom country residence. Police said the property was unoccupied at the time. The late Queen Elizabeth II gave Anmer Hall to the couple as a wedding present in 2011. They use it for holidays and short breaks, while their main residence is Forest Lodge on the Windsor estate. Norfolk Police said they are continuing to investigate. A Kensington Palace representative said the couple’s office would not comment on security matters.
world.image_alt: Two men arrested after suspected break-in at Prince William’s Norfolk home

business.title: Dell raises fiscal 2027 outlook as AI-server orders hit $132 billion
business.summary: Dell Technologies raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $202 billion from $192 billion after third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $54.94 billion, beating analysts’ estimates. Adjusted earnings reached $9.45 per share, and Dell lifted its forecast for AI-optimized server revenue to $78 billion. Its AI-server
business.content: Dell Technologies raised its fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $202 billion from $192 billion after third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $54.94 billion, beating analysts’ estimates. Adjusted earnings reached $9.45 per share, and Dell lifted its forecast for AI-optimized server revenue to $78 billion. Its AI-server backlog reached a record $132.3 billion after $60.2 billion in orders during the quarter. The infrastructure business drove the gains, while Dell’s PC revenue rose 3% and fell short of forecasts. The company also authorized another $25 billion in share repurchases. For the current quarter, Dell forecast revenue of $56.3 billion and adjusted earnings of $8.40 per share. It expects memory-chip supply constraints to continue into 2027 and said its infrastructure operating margin could dip below 15% as lower-margin AI servers account for more sales.
business.image_alt: Dell raises fiscal 2027 outlook as AI-server orders hit $132 billion

business.title: U.S. soybean futures climb as Trump cites new China buying deal
business.summary: U.S. soybean futures rose for a third straight session on Tuesday, Nov. 24, after President Donald Trump said he had reached a new trade deal with China involving increased soybean purchases; traders said no details had been published. January soybeans closed at $12.34 a bushel, up 0.42%, while March futures settled at
business.content: U.S. soybean futures rose for a third straight session on Tuesday, Nov. 24, after President Donald Trump said he had reached a new trade deal with China involving increased soybean purchases; traders said no details had been published. January soybeans closed at $12.34 a bushel, up 0.42%, while March futures settled at $12.37¼. The move also lifted Brazilian cash prices in several markets, with port prices reaching their highest levels of the year, though physical trading was quiet. The U.S. Department of Agriculture forecasts a record 4.5 billion-bushel crop and record soybean crushing of 2.78 billion bushels, while export sales are off to their strongest start in four years. U.S. tariff announcements followed Trump’s comments, and market adviser Mark Knight of Farmer’s Keeper Financial said traders lacked details on the claimed deal.
business.image_alt: U.S. soybean futures climb as Trump cites new China buying deal

business.title: Judge orders former OpenAI engineer released on $1 million bond
business.summary: U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex Tse ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan released on a $1 million bond Tuesday, reversing an earlier decision to keep him jailed while he faces a charge of secretly intercepting oral communications. Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, pleaded not guilty; prosecutors allege he
business.content: U.S. Magistrate Judge Alex Tse ordered former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan released on a $1 million bond Tuesday, reversing an earlier decision to keep him jailed while he faces a charge of secretly intercepting oral communications. Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, pleaded not guilty; prosecutors allege he hid a recording device in an executive conference room at the artificial intelligence company’s San Francisco headquarters. Before he can be released, Alfozan must post $500,000 in cash, with three friends guaranteeing the rest. His lawyer said he expected Alfozan to be released Wednesday and planned to seek a trial delay; jury selection is scheduled to begin Jan. 20, 2027. Prosecutors opposed release, arguing that Alfozan could flee; Tse said the government had not presented sufficient evidence to justify holding him on a corporate-espionage theory.
business.image_alt: Judge orders former OpenAI engineer released on $1 million bond

business.title: Utah seeks to drop Kalshi charges after platform halts trading
business.summary: Utah has asked a state court to dismiss 14 criminal charges against prediction-market operator Kalshi and co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara after the company stopped accepting new trades from Utah residents. The charges alleged illegal gambling. The state seeks dismissal without prejudice, allowing prosecu
business.content: Utah has asked a state court to dismiss 14 criminal charges against prediction-market operator Kalshi and co-founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara after the company stopped accepting new trades from Utah residents. The charges alleged illegal gambling. The state seeks dismissal without prejudice, allowing prosecutors to refile if Kalshi returns. A judge must still approve the request. The executives had been scheduled to appear in court on Dec. 4. Kalshi halted new trading after a federal judge declined to block Utah’s enforcement of its gambling laws while a federal case over regulatory authority proceeds. Kalshi and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission argue that the platform’s event contracts fall under federal commodities law, while Utah and other states say sports-related contracts constitute gambling subject to state law. Utah’s separate civil case seeking Kalshi’s profits continues, and the company says it will continue challenging the state’s authority.
business.image_alt: Utah seeks to drop Kalshi charges after platform halts trading

business.title: U.S. tariff plan could raise import costs across 16 economies
business.summary: The Trump administration is preparing country-specific tariffs on imports from 16 economies. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to release findings from an investigation into alleged industrial subsidies and excess production. The proposed duties would be added to existing tariffs, but trade-deal caps
business.content: The Trump administration is preparing country-specific tariffs on imports from 16 economies. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to release findings from an investigation into alleged industrial subsidies and excess production. The proposed duties would be added to existing tariffs, but trade-deal caps are expected to limit rates for some suppliers. The reported ceilings are 15% for the European Union, Japan and South Korea, 19% for Malaysia, and 20% for China if its trade truce with Washington is extended. Tariffs of 10% to 12.5% imposed in July over alleged failures to curb forced-labor goods also apply. Oil, gas, fertilizer and some products already subject to national-security duties are expected to be excluded. The new measures are expected to target mostly manufactured goods, but officials have not disclosed the final product lists or rates. Trade expert Deborah Elms estimated that the additional duties could range from 2% to 7.5% if the aim is to restore earlier tariff levels while honoring agreements. Affected economies will have opportunities for hearings and public comment before final rates are set.
business.image_alt: U.S. tariff plan could raise import costs across 16 economies

business.title: AI investment drives U.S. growth, complicating Fed
business.summary: Artificial intelligence investment has become a major contributor to U.S. economic growth through spending on data centers, chips, computing equipment, power systems and cooling. It has also boosted activity among businesses serving construction projects. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has called AI central to U.S. leadership,
business.content: Artificial intelligence investment has become a major contributor to U.S. economic growth through spending on data centers, chips, computing equipment, power systems and cooling. It has also boosted activity among businesses serving construction projects. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has called AI central to U.S. leadership, while the central bank faces strong inflation data and financial markets signaling weaker inflation expectations. Hotels near data centers have reported revenue growth, and snowmobile maker Polaris has reported demand from contractors building data centers. Evercore ISI Vice President Krishna Guha, a former Federal Reserve Bank of New York official, said the Fed must avoid both undermining its inflation credibility and being seen as having halted the AI boom. Separately, Seeking Alpha analyst Nicolas Bolsinger argues that rapid capital spending and credit links among AI infrastructure firms could spread financial stress if growth falters. His assessment is based on his own credit-risk model, not an official forecast.
business.image_alt: AI investment drives U.S. growth, complicating Fed

business.title: Huawei verdict raises risk of billions in penalties
business.summary: A New York jury convicted Chinese telecommunications supplier Huawei on 10 criminal counts, potentially exposing it to billions of dollars in penalties. The company is already barred from selling equipment to U.S. carriers. The jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice; no exec
business.content: A New York jury convicted Chinese telecommunications supplier Huawei on 10 criminal counts, potentially exposing it to billions of dollars in penalties. The company is already barred from selling equipment to U.S. carriers. The jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice; no executives or employees were tried in the Brooklyn case. Huawei sells smartphones and telecom equipment internationally, operates in about 170 countries and employs more than 200,000 people, according to its lawyer and court reports. The company has also expanded into semiconductor manufacturing as China seeks alternatives to Nvidia chips to meet demand for artificial intelligence. The verdict’s effect on Huawei’s overseas business remains uncertain. Sentencing is scheduled for Sept. 14, 2027, and Huawei says it expects to appeal.
business.image_alt: Huawei verdict raises risk of billions in penalties

business.title: Sanofi agrees to $41 billion Insmed deal to offset Dupixent patent cliff
business.summary: French drugmaker Sanofi has agreed to buy U.S. biotech Insmed for $41 billion in cash, or $175 a share, as it seeks growth ahead of the expected 2031 loss of U.S. patent protection for Dupixent, its best-selling medicine. Dupixent generated more than €15 billion in 2025, nearly 40% of Sanofi’s revenue. Insmed has two m
business.content: French drugmaker Sanofi has agreed to buy U.S. biotech Insmed for $41 billion in cash, or $175 a share, as it seeks growth ahead of the expected 2031 loss of U.S. patent protection for Dupixent, its best-selling medicine. Dupixent generated more than €15 billion in 2025, nearly 40% of Sanofi’s revenue. Insmed has two marketed respiratory medicines and a late-stage pipeline. Sanofi expects the deal to generate more than $500 million in annual cost savings and increase adjusted earnings per share by the end of 2028. The companies expect to complete the deal in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder approval and regulatory clearances in the United States and abroad.
business.image_alt: Sanofi agrees to $41 billion Insmed deal to offset Dupixent patent cliff

science.title: Researchers find evidence of p-wave magnetism in europium silicide
science.summary: Researchers report evidence that europium silicide (EuSi), a metallic compound, hosts an unusual magnetic state called p-wave magnetism, in which electron spin polarization depends on the direction electrons travel. Between about 33 and 62 kelvin, europium atoms form a repeating spiral whose magnetic moments cancel ove
science.content: Researchers report evidence that europium silicide (EuSi), a metallic compound, hosts an unusual magnetic state called p-wave magnetism, in which electron spin polarization depends on the direction electrons travel. Between about 33 and 62 kelvin, europium atoms form a repeating spiral whose magnetic moments cancel overall but still strongly alter the electrons’ energy levels. Neutron diffraction and photoemission measurements found energy separations exceeding 100 millielectronvolts and spin-polarization reversals across successive magnetic Brillouin zones. The researchers also identified magnetic domains of opposite handedness about 10 micrometers across. The results support a proposed p-wave magnetic state, but predicted effects such as current without an external magnetic field and unconventional superconductivity have not been directly demonstrated in EuSi.
science.image_alt: Researchers find evidence of p-wave magnetism in europium silicide

science.title: Australia awards top science prize to melanoma oncologist and physicist
science.summary: Australia jointly awarded its 2026 Prime Minister’s Prize for Science to oncologist Professor Georgina Long and physicist Professor Anthony Thomas at a ceremony in Canberra on Tuesday night. Long’s research led to effective melanoma drug therapies, while Thomas was recognized for work on protons, neutron stars and dark
science.content: Australia jointly awarded its 2026 Prime Minister’s Prize for Science to oncologist Professor Georgina Long and physicist Professor Anthony Thomas at a ceremony in Canberra on Tuesday night. Long’s research led to effective melanoma drug therapies, while Thomas was recognized for work on protons, neutron stars and dark matter. Among other recipients, Professor Asha Bowen received the life scientist award for research that helped deliver the first significant reduction in skin infections among Aboriginal children in 50 years. Professor Mark Smythe won the innovation prize for turning Australian research into medicines approved to treat conditions including psoriasis and a blood cancer.
science.image_alt: Australia awards top science prize to melanoma oncologist and physicist

science.title: Army prepares Iowa lead azide blast as scientists plan air sampling
science.summary: The U.S. Army says it will detonate about 9,700 pounds of degraded lead azide at its ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at 9 a.m. Wednesday, as scientists prepare to measure lead dust from the blast. The operation targets 68 aging barrels that the Army says could explode spontaneously as temperatures fall. Current f
science.content: The U.S. Army says it will detonate about 9,700 pounds of degraded lead azide at its ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at 9 a.m. Wednesday, as scientists prepare to measure lead dust from the blast. The operation targets 68 aging barrels that the Army says could explode spontaneously as temperatures fall. Current forecasts indicate the plume could travel southwest, potentially more than 100 miles. Researchers from the University of Iowa and other institutions are setting up independent air sampling to compare post-blast readings with background lead levels. One University of Iowa team has established about 18 monitoring sites extending roughly 40 kilometers southwest of the plant. Scientists say the plume’s reach will depend partly on particle size and weather. Officials say the Army will use barriers, foam, gels and water to limit dust, then test air, soil and water to identify where lead settles. Officials are offering relocation help to residents within a five-mile southwest evacuation zone and have told people farther away to shelter indoors. The independent university data are expected late next week.
science.image_alt: Army prepares Iowa lead azide blast as scientists plan air sampling

science.title: California king tides break November record as coastal flood threat grows
science.summary: King tides flooded low-lying parts of California on Tuesday, Nov. 24, as water at San Francisco’s Crissy Field reached 8.23 feet, topping the November record of 7.97 feet set in 1982. Forecasters expected tides to rise further Wednesday and Thursday, with heavy rain and storm surge adding to the coastal flood risk. Sev
science.content: King tides flooded low-lying parts of California on Tuesday, Nov. 24, as water at San Francisco’s Crissy Field reached 8.23 feet, topping the November record of 7.97 feet set in 1982. Forecasters expected tides to rise further Wednesday and Thursday, with heavy rain and storm surge adding to the coastal flood risk. Several factors contributed to the flooding: the annual high tides, warm water associated with a strong El Niño, storm surge and a higher baseline sea level. Southern California’s sea level has risen 20 to 30 centimeters over the past century; a strong El Niño can add another 15 to 30 centimeters for months. The National Weather Service warned of breaking waves reaching 20 to 30 feet and hazardous beach conditions, while local officials reported flooding and ordered some coastal evacuations. Further king-tide cycles are expected around Christmas and Jan. 21-22.
science.image_alt: California king tides break November record as coastal flood threat grows

science.title: Archaeological studies trace ancient diets and Roman Britain’s diversity
science.summary: Three separate archaeological studies offer new evidence about past diets and migration. A study of “Rodhals Man,” excavated in 1956, describes him as a rare source of evidence about the shift toward farming. Research at two sites in Western Australia challenges the idea that ancient people widened their diets only whe
science.content: Three separate archaeological studies offer new evidence about past diets and migration. A study of “Rodhals Man,” excavated in 1956, describes him as a rare source of evidence about the shift toward farming. Research at two sites in Western Australia challenges the idea that ancient people widened their diets only when preferred foods became scarce. A study of cremated remains from Colchester, Britain’s first Roman capital, found that some residents had origins in the Mediterranean, including Italy, Spain and Lebanon. The researchers used strontium and lead isotope ratios in dense skull bone to trace the origins of people whose cremated remains would otherwise be difficult to study.
science.image_alt: Archaeological studies trace ancient diets and Roman Britain’s diversity

science.title: Euclid finds quasar with 360-million-solar-mass black hole from the early universe
science.summary: Astronomers have identified the most distant known quasar, J1504+6252, whose light dates to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Its central black hole has about 360 million times the sun’s mass, and its light dates to roughly 40 million years earlier than that of the previous record-holder. The team first found
science.content: Astronomers have identified the most distant known quasar, J1504+6252, whose light dates to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. Its central black hole has about 360 million times the sun’s mass, and its light dates to roughly 40 million years earlier than that of the previous record-holder. The team first found the object in observations from the European Space Agency’s Euclid telescope. Follow-up measurements, including observations with the James Webb Space Telescope, established its distance and mass. Observations indicate the black hole is now accreting material relatively slowly. To explain its mass, researchers are considering whether it grew much faster earlier or began as a massive “direct-collapse” black hole rather than the remnant of a star. The study, led by astronomer Julien Wolf, was published in Astronomy & Astrophysics. Researchers say further Euclid discoveries could test explanations for how early quasars formed.
science.image_alt: Euclid finds quasar with 360-million-solar-mass black hole from the early universe

science.title: Tiny solar tracker records hummingbird’s 4,055-mile migration to Alaska
science.summary: Researchers used miniature solar-powered transmitters to track a male Rufous hummingbird from Alabama to Alaska, recording a 4,055-mile journey in 38 days—the longest hummingbird migration documented to date. They tagged the bird in Lillian, Alabama, on March 27, 2025, and it reached Juneau on May 3. The team fitted 11
science.content: Researchers used miniature solar-powered transmitters to track a male Rufous hummingbird from Alabama to Alaska, recording a 4,055-mile journey in 38 days—the longest hummingbird migration documented to date. They tagged the bird in Lillian, Alabama, on March 27, 2025, and it reached Juneau on May 3. The team fitted 11 hummingbirds with the devices in coastal Alabama and Florida in spring 2025 to track their movements across North America. The study authors said Rufous and ruby-throated hummingbird populations have recently declined; further research is needed to assess any long-term effects of wearing the transmitters.
science.image_alt: Tiny solar tracker records hummingbird’s 4,055-mile migration to Alaska

science.title: England records 5,258 heat-linked deaths after record-hot summer
science.summary: England recorded an estimated 5,258 deaths associated with extreme heat between May and September 2026, the highest total since the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) began monitoring in 2016 and nearly twice the previous record of 2,985 in 2022. The figures are provisional because death-registration data for the period
science.content: England recorded an estimated 5,258 deaths associated with extreme heat between May and September 2026, the highest total since the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) began monitoring in 2016 and nearly twice the previous record of 2,985 in 2022. The figures are provisional because death-registration data for the period are incomplete. The agency counted seven heat episodes lasting a total of 41 days, both records since monitoring began. The deadliest stretch was June 21-28, when heat was associated with an estimated 2,401 deaths; more than 3,000 deaths were linked to episodes in May and June combined. Heat can trigger heatstroke and dehydration or worsen cardiovascular and respiratory conditions. Dr Ross Thompson, UKHSA’s principal environmental health scientist, said periods of extreme heat are expected to become longer, more frequent and more intense as the climate warms.
science.image_alt: England records 5,258 heat-linked deaths after record-hot summer

sports.title: Tottenham sign 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett to long-term deal
sports.summary: Tottenham Hotspur have signed 18-year-old academy player Luca Williams-Barnett to a new long-term contract, three days after he scored a goal and set up another in his first Premier League start, a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town. Tottenham did not disclose the contract’s length; his previous deal was reported to run until 2
sports.content: Tottenham Hotspur have signed 18-year-old academy player Luca Williams-Barnett to a new long-term contract, three days after he scored a goal and set up another in his first Premier League start, a 2-0 win over Ipswich Town. Tottenham did not disclose the contract’s length; his previous deal was reported to run until 2028. Williams-Barnett opened the scoring after 15 minutes and set up Dominic Solanke’s goal shortly after half-time. Williams-Barnett became Tottenham’s youngest Premier League scorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 and the league’s second-youngest player to score and assist in one match, after Michael Owen. His performances had reportedly drawn interest from Chelsea and Borussia Dortmund. Sports Mole said he was expected to remain in Tottenham’s starting lineup for Sunday’s match against Sunderland.

sports.content: Jannik Sinner, the world No. 2 tennis player, underwent minor surgery on his right knee on Tuesday to address an iliotibial-band problem after months of treatment failed to resolve it. He has not played since winning Wimbledon on July 12 and had hoped to return for the Australian Open, which starts January 17 in Melbourne. Italian sports media and a knee specialist have estimated recovery at three to four months. Sinner has not announced a return date, and his participation in Melbourne remains in doubt. Sinner won Wimbledon and five consecutive Masters 1000 titles this season. His absence has helped Alexander Zverev take the world No. 1 ranking, while Carlos Alcaraz is the reigning Australian Open champion. Sinner said he will begin rehabilitation with his team. It is unclear whether he will recover in time for the American hard-court swing at Indian Wells and Miami.

sports.content: Portsmouth beat West Ham United 1-0 at Fratton Park on Tuesday, extending Scott Parker’s winless start as West Ham manager to four games and the Hammers’ run without a victory to six. Odin Bailey scored in the 31st minute after West Ham goalkeeper Finlay Herrick failed to clear Tyrese Shade’s cross. West Ham hit the woodwork twice but could not equalize. The defeat left West Ham 12th, 11 points behind the Championship leaders, while Portsmouth climbed to 10th. West Ham had been the division’s leading scorers but failed to score for the first time this season. Parker said his side were “too easy to score against” and accepted that they had not been unlucky. West Ham next visit Stoke on Saturday.

sports.content: Galatasaray substitute Deniz Gül headed in the winner in the 77th minute as the hosts beat Aston Villa 1-0 in Istanbul, handing the English side a second straight Champions League defeat and extending their winless run in all competitions to six matches. Villa failed to register a shot on target; Gül’s goal was the match’s first effort on target. The result left both clubs on nine points after five league-phase matches, but Villa slipped to ninth on goal difference and Galatasaray rose to 13th. Villa had won their first three games before losing at Barcelona and Galatasaray; the top eight qualify directly for the knockout phase, while teams outside it face a playoff. Villa’s upcoming European fixtures include Paris Saint-Germain at home and Borussia Dortmund. Galatasaray’s next league-phase match is away to AEK on December 8, while Villa travel to Ipswich next in domestic competition.

sports.content: Real Madrid came from behind to beat PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday, with England midfielder Jude Bellingham scoring a volley after coming on at halftime and Kylian Mbappé adding two goals. Ivan Perišić put PSV ahead from the penalty spot in the first half. Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the break, and Bellingham struck in the 60th minute before Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior completed the scoring. Madrid’s fifth win in five Champions League league-phase matches put them top of the table with 15 points. Madrid had struggled to contain PSV before coach José Mourinho made three changes at halftime, including bringing on Bellingham. Bellingham has scored four goals in his last five club appearances and said Mourinho’s confidence and the freedom to move across midfield have helped his form. Elsewhere, Arsenal drew 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli, and Aston Villa lost 1-0 to Galatasaray. Madrid’s next European match is away to Arsenal on December 9.

sports.content: England beat Australia by eight wickets in the second T20 international on the Gold Coast, chasing 185 in 13.1 overs to level the five-match series at 1-1. Welsh-born openers Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt put on 151 runs in 10.1 overs: Donald made 85 from 32 balls and Salt scored 58 from 30. England finished on 188-2 with 41 balls unused. Australia made 184-8 after choosing to bat, recovering from 58-4 as Nikhil Chaudhary scored 45 and Joel Davies added 39. Ben Dwarshuis hit sixes off the last three balls of the innings, but England reached the target with more than six overs to spare. The third match is scheduled for Friday, November 27, at the Gabba in Brisbane; two more fixtures follow in Sydney and Canberra.

sports.content: Liverpool midfielder Florian Wirtz says he is in the best form of his Anfield career after a difficult first season following his £116 million move from Bayer Leverkusen in 2025. He scored and provided an assist in Liverpool’s 4-0 win over Manchester United on Nov. 22 and has five goals and two assists in his last four appearances for club and country. Wirtz credits head coach Andoni Iraola’s confidence in him, his improved physical condition and his growing familiarity with English football. He also says Germany coach Jürgen Klopp, Liverpool’s former manager, gives him private advice about succeeding at the club. Liverpool travel to face Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday, Nov. 25. They have nine points from four matches, having won their first three before losing to Fenerbahce. Brugge have 10 wins and a draw in their last 11 games, including a 4-3 victory over Inter last month.

He reached 100 in 28 balls and 200 in 52, hitting 28 sixes and seven fours before be
sports.content: India A batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 from 53 balls against the United Arab Emirates in Doha on Tuesday, setting List A records for the fastest century, 150 and double-century and the most sixes in a senior men’s innings. He reached 100 in 28 balls and 200 in 52, hitting 28 sixes and seven fours before being caught with India A five runs short of victory. India A chased down the UAE’s 249-8 in 14.2 overs, winning by seven wickets in the Asia Cup Rising Stars group match. Sooryavanshi’s 52-ball double-century nearly halved the previous List A record of 103 balls, while his hundred beat the 29-ball mark. Sooryavanshi made his debut for India’s senior T20 side in July. India A has reached the Rising Stars semi-finals, scheduled for Thursday and Friday, with the final on Sunday.
